raw_segments.text: We leave the Delian ports and put to sea. By Naxos, fammed for vintage, make our way,
then green Donasa pass, and sail in sight of Paros Isle with marble quarries white.
We pass the scattered isles of cichlides that, scarce distinguished, seem to stud the seas.
The shouts of sailors double near the shores, they stretch their canvas, and they ply their
oars. All hands aloft for Crete, for Crete. They cry, and swiftly throw, the foamy billows
fly. Full on the promised land at length we bore, with joy descending on the Cretan shore.
With eager haste a rising town I frame, which from the Trojan Pergamos I name. The name
itself was grateful. I exhort to found their houses, and erect a fort.
Our ships are hauled upon the yellow strand, the youth begin to till the labored land,
and I myself new marriages promote, give laws and dwellings I divide by lot. When rising
vapors choke the wholesome air, and blasts of noisome winds corrupt the year, the trees
devouring caterpillars burn. Parched was the grass, and blighted was the corn. Nor scape
the beasts, for serious from on high, with pestilential heat infects the sky. My men,
some fall, the rest in fevers fry. Again my father bids me seek the shore of
